candidates.title: Great White Fleet splits Central America–US service
candidates.excerpt: Chiquita’s Great White Fleet will restructure its Central America–United States network from December, according to DynaLiners. The carrier will remove Port Everglades from its USSE service and transfer the Florida call to the new Port Everglades–Wilmington service, branded PEWI. The new PEWI service will operate weekly with two container ships of approximately 1,800 TEUs each. The revised rotations will be: - USSE: Puerto Barrios – Puerto Cortés – Puerto Barrios – Gulfport – Freeport, Texas – Puerto Barrios - PEWI: Puerto Barrios – Puerto Cortés – Port Everglades – Wilmington, Delaware – Puerto Barrios The restructuring separates Great White Fleet’s Gulf Coast and US East Coast coverage into two dedicated loops.

candidates.title: MSC extends Shikra service to Khor Fakkan and Sohar
candidates.excerpt: MSC has extended its Far East–India Shikra service to the Middle East by adding calls at Khor Fakkan in the United Arab Emirates and Sohar in Oman. The revised service will provide direct connections between major Chinese ports, Singapore, India and the Gulf. MSC will increase the Shikra deployment to 15 containerships with capacities ranging from approximately 14,000 to 24,300 TEU. The revised rotation will be: Dalian – Tianjin – Qingdao – Shanghai – Ningbo – Nansha – Singapore – Nhava Sheva – Mundra – Khor Fakkan – Sohar – Dalian The addition of Khor Fakkan and Sohar expands Shikra beyond its previous Far East–India coverage, adding direct access to two major Middle Eastern container gateways.

candidates.title: Two new quay cranes strengthen port Botany’s capability
candidates.excerpt: Hutchison Ports Sydney is now operating two new ship-to-shore cranes at its Port Botany terminal. The cranes are designed to serve vessels carrying more than 15,000 TEU, with each able to reach across ships up to 23 containers wide and to work containers stacked more than nine high above deck. The investment responds to the continuing growth in the size of global container ships. It improves Port Botany’s ability to accommodate larger vessels and gives shipping lines greater flexibility on Australian trade routes. The largest container ships now serving Australia have a capacity of around 9,000 TEU, so the new cranes will allow the port to handle ships 50 percent larger. NSW Ports CEO Marika Calfas welcomed the arrival of the cranes as a significant investment in the future of the state’s container port, saying that the ability to service the largest vessels calling at Port Botany helps improve supply chain efficiency and keeps New South Wales well placed for growing global trade. candidates.title: UP No. 5511 begins steam testing
candidates.excerpt: SILVIS, Ill. — Union Pacific 2-10-2 No. 5511 was steamed up today (Friday, Nov. 6) by Railroading Heritage of Midwest America. It is the first time the locomotive has been under steam since 1956. The locomotive, built by Baldwin in 1923, is the sole remaining UP 2-10-2. RRHMA began an extensive rebuilding project after the engine was donated by UP in 2022. The locomotive was retired in 1956, and was last used that year as a stationary boiler for an industry in Ogden, Utah. It was used in filming the Union Pacific motion picture “Last of the Giants” in 1958, but was not under steam at that time. It was then stored in Green River, Wyo., until it was transferred to the UP roundhouse in Cheyenne, Wyo., in 1968. The locomotive, which underwent a hydrostatic test on Sept. 8, was pulled outside the Silvis facility and steamed up for testing. RRHMA has not announced any immediate plans to operate the 2-10-2. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com.

candidates.excerpt: 2 exh991pressrelease9302026.htm Document FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Trinity Industries, Inc. (NYSE:TRN) today announced earnings results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Financial and Operational Highlights – Third Quarter • Quarterly total company revenues of $535 million • Quarterly income from continuing operations per common diluted share ("EPS") of $0.27 • Lease fleet utilization of 97.0% and Future Lease Rate Differential ("FLRD") of 0.1% at quarter-end • New railcar orders of 2,190 and railcar deliveries of 2,030 • Year
